Dyna-Q: learning and planning

Q-learning uses each real experience once and throws it away. Dyna-Q also stores it in a model: "in this state, this action led there, with this reward". Between real steps it replays remembered transitions and applies the same Q-learning update to them. Planning is learning from imagined experience.

The maths

Each real step of tabular Dyna-Q does three things. With $S$ the current state:

$$\begin{aligned} &\text{1. Act: } A \leftarrow \varepsilon\text{-greedy}(S, Q), \ \text{observe } R, S' \\ &\text{2. Learn: } Q(S, A) \leftarrow Q(S, A) + \alpha\big[R + \gamma \max_a Q(S', a) - Q(S, A)\big] \\ &\text{3. Remember: } \mathit{Model}(S, A) \leftarrow (R, S') \end{aligned}$$

Then it plans, repeating $n$ times:

$$\begin{aligned} &\tilde S \leftarrow \text{a random previously visited state}, \quad \tilde A \leftarrow \text{a random action previously taken in } \tilde S \\ &(\tilde R, \tilde S') \leftarrow \mathit{Model}(\tilde S, \tilde A) \\ &Q(\tilde S, \tilde A) \leftarrow Q(\tilde S, \tilde A) + \alpha\big[\tilde R + \gamma \max_a Q(\tilde S', a) - Q(\tilde S, \tilde A)\big] \end{aligned}$$

The planning update is the Q-learning update (Lesson 52) applied to remembered transitions. The maze is deterministic, so the model can store the single outcome it saw. Both kinds of update improve the same $Q$, so the agent cannot tell real from imagined progress.

Why it helps. With all $Q = 0$ and reward only at G, plain Q-learning ($n = 0$) finishes its first episode having changed exactly one value: the last step into G, to $\alpha \cdot 1 = 0.1$. Each later episode pushes that information back about one more step. With planning, every remembered transition next to a valued state can pick up value in the same real step, so the value spreads back along the whole remembered path within a few steps of the second episode.

The values it is heading for: one step before G, $q_*$ is $1$. Each step further back multiplies by $\gamma$, so a state $k$ steps from G has

$$v_*(s) = \gamma^{\,k-1}$$

Dyna is the simplest form of model-based RL. Its model is a lookup table of what happened. Lesson 97 returns to agents that learn richer models and plan inside them.
